encounters.cc: Worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea requiring sleeping upright

lines: Worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea requiring sleeping upright

This 71-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, anemia of chronic kidney disease, and history of tuberculosis and severe hypoglycemia presents to the emergency department with worsening shortness of breath that began two days ago and has progressively worsened.
He now struggles to walk across the room without becoming winded and has been sleeping upright in a recliner due to severe breathlessness when lying flat.
He also reports a 5-pound weight gain and reduced urine output over the past week.
His medical history includes end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Left upper extremity arteriovenous fistula creation
- Right internal jugular dialysis catheter placement (historical)
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro Sliding scale subcutaneous with meals
- Sevelamer carbonate 800 mg PO with meals
He missed his last two scheduled dialysis sessions due to transportation issues.
Temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure is 172/94 mm Hg, pulse is 106/min, and respiratory rate is 28/min.
On exam, he appears visibly uncomfortable and dyspneic.
Jugular venous distension is noted 10 cm above the sternal angle.
Lung auscultation reveals diffuse bilateral crackles.
Cardiac exam reveals a third heart sound.
There is moderate bilateral pitting edema in the lower extremities.
Arterial blood gas shows hypoxemia with a widened A–a gradient.
Chest x-ray shows an enlarged cardiac silhouette and bilateral perihilar alveolar infiltrates.
ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy and sinus tachycardia.
He is placed on oxygen and started on intravenous furosemide.

encounters.cc: Progressive difficulty walking with magnetic gait and short shuffling steps

lines: Progressive difficulty walking with magnetic gait and short shuffling steps

The patient is a 74-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on maintenance hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension, last evaluated for dialysis-related amyloidosis one year ago, who presents to the neurology clinic for assessment of gait changes.
He is accompanied by his daughter, who reports progressive difficulty walking over the past 6 months.
She describes his gait as "magnetic," with short, shuffling steps and difficulty initiating movement.
Additionally, she notes that he has become increasingly forgetful and has had episodes of urinary incontinence.
- Sepsis secondary to vascular access-related bacteremia (diagnosed 2024-01-15)
His past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Left upper extremity arteriovenous fistula creation
- Right internal jugular dialysis catheter placement (historical)
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro Sliding scale subcutaneous with meals
- Sevelamer carbonate 800 mg PO with meals
Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 10 years ago.
On examination, the patient is alert but oriented only to person and place.
Cranial nerves are intact, and strength is 5/5 in all extremities.
A CT scan of the head shows enlarged ventricles with no evidence of cortical atrophy.
Lumbar puncture reveals an opening pressure within normal limits, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis is unremarkable.
